issues.description: The problem statement's UML declares Stock.add(String) as returning void, but both the template and the solution implement Stock.add(String) to return an int. This mismatch can confuse students about the expected return type and what the method should do (e.g., whether it reports the new quantity or not).
issues.suggestedFix: Make the problem statement UML consistent with the code: change the UML entry for Stock.add(String) to +add(String): int and document the return value (e.g., returns the new quantity or -1 on failure). Alternatively, change the template/solution implementation to return void, but updating the UML to int is recommended to match existing code and tests.
